validity.recommendation: Correct SegmentCost from 429,900,000 USD to 492,900,000 USD -- current value is almost certainly a digit transposition (429.9 <-> 492.9). Every dated primary source (both from Sept 2009, at commissioning) states the total project cost as US$492.9 million, and both give the same internal breakdown: $417.9M from Uzbekneftegaz's own funds + $75M credit from the Fund for Reconstruction and Development of Uzbekistan = $492.9M exactly. No source anywhere states $429.9M.
validity.researcher_notes: Read the sheet's own cited SegmentCost ref (uzdaily.uz/en/post/6945/, trailing slash) first per the standing instruction -- it verifies live but does NOT contain the sheet's value 429,900,000 in any form (existing_ref_checks already flagged this: '200 but data value not found'). Fetched the page directly: it is a genuine Sept 8 2009 news article ('Uzbekneftegaz to launch Ahangaran-Pungan gas pipeline in September') and it states cost = US$492.9 million, financed by $417.9M own resources + $75M FRDU credit, length 165 km, capacity 10 bcm/y, general contractor Zeromax GmbH, route via the Kamchik pass (2,268 m). A second, independently-bylined 2009 outlet (gazeta.uz, dated one day earlier, 2009-09-07, 'Gaz dlya doliny poydet cherez Kamchik') reports the identical three headline numbers (492.9M USD / 165 km / 10 bcm/y) and adds that the compressor station maintaining pipeline pressure was built in Ahangaran. Both articles are almost certainly downstream of one official Uzbekneftegaz/UzA announcement (identical figures to one decimal, published within a day of each other) -- treating this as ONE origin (medium tier), not two independent sources, per the wire-story rule. EXISTENCE: confirmed real and currently operating -- see status_reviews (Sept 2025 evidence: gas supply on this exact named trunk was deliberately suspended for 36 hours to tie in a new ~22 km section). CLASSIFICATION: correct as transmission gas pipeline -- every source calls it a 'magistral'nyy gazoprovod' (main/trunk gas pipeline). LENGTH (165 km) and CAPACITY (10 bcm/y) both match the sheet exactly and are corroborated (see fills). DUPLICATE CHECK against the roster: P4072 (same name, 25.0 km, dia 1020, status operating) is NOT the same physical pipe as P4071 -- it is a separate loop/parallel line on the high-mountain section, first reported under construction in a 2020 EPSILON(EDC) press item ('15 avgusta nachato stroitel'stvo lupinga na vysokogornom uchastke ... Akhangaran-Pungan, protyazhennost'yu 25 km', uzreport.news / kun.uz, both 2020-09-09) and only completed and tied in five years later (gazeta.uz + spot.uz, both 2025-09-04/06: 'pochti 22 km dopolnitel'nogo gazoprovoda' connected on the mountain section). The ~25 km planned vs ~22 km as-built is a normal design-vs-built variance, not a conflict. So P4071 = the original 2009, 165 km trunk; P4072 = its 2020-2025 loop -- two genuinely distinct pipes, not a double count. OWNER (Uztransgaz 100%): plausible but NOT independently pinned to this specific pipeline -- UzTransGas JSC (est. 1992, Cabinet of Ministers decree No. 585) is Uzbekistan's sole state operator for gas transmission/transit nationwide, and the 2020 EPSILON item lists repair works organized under Uztransgaz's regional 'UMG' (Directorate of Main Gas Pipelines) subdivisions, but no source found names an 'Akhangaran UMG' or otherwise ties Uztransgaz by name to THIS pipeline specifically. Left UNRESOLVED rather than citing a generic corporate-history page that never mentions Ahangaran-Pungan by name (see fills). LOCATION: Ahangaran (Tashkent region) confirmed as the start/compressor-station end by both 2009 sources; 'Pungan' as the Fergana-side terminus is corroborated only by consistent use in the pipeline's own name and by every source's framing ('to improve gas supply to the Fergana Valley') -- no source pinpoints Pungan as a distinct named facility beyond the pipeline's title. utg.uz's own pages for this pipeline (history, investitsionnye-proekty) are all confirmed HTTP 404 -- the whole utg.uz subsite appears to have been restructured (only the bare root https://utg.uz/ still resolves); could not reach web.archive.org today (2026-08-26) to check for a snapshot -- consistent with the country note's known outage, a network condition, not evidence the page is gone for good.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status = operating is strongly and recently confirmed, not just unchanged from the sheet's last touch. Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy announced (press service statement, carried near-identically by gazeta.uz 2025-09-04, spot.uz 2025-09-06, and uzdaily.uz's Russian edition) that natural gas supply through the named 'Ahangaran-Pungan' trunk was deliberately suspended for 36 hours starting 12:00 on 2025-09-05 specifically to tie in a new, almost-22-km additional section on the pipeline's mountain segment, aimed at improving winter supply reliability to Fergana Valley consumers; supply to Andijan resumed 2025-09-06 20:00 and to Fergana/Namangan at 21:00. This is unambiguous, dated evidence the pipeline is physically real and actively carrying gas today, not merely a book entry. Treating the three outlets as one origin (all explicitly cite 'press-sluzhba Ministerstva energetiki') for tier purposes -- medium, not high -- but the underlying event itself is not in doubt. Also found a 2020 predecessor item (uzreport.news / kun.uz, 2020-09-09, EPSILON EDC) reporting the START of construction on this same loop ('lupinga ... protyazhennost'yu 25 km' on the pipeline's high-mountain section), which is corroborating continuity evidence (2009 commissioning -> 2020 loop start -> 2025 loop completion) rather than an independent status data point, so not counted separately.
